author: @belight2612
text: Not really. Kpop is any popular music in South Korea and it can be any type of music. SEVENTEEN, for one, has a very diverse discography. If I want to introduce non-kpop fans to SEVENTEEN by recommending a song, I would have consider their tastes. If they like dance anthems, maybe Hit or Super. If they like ballads, Don't Wanna Cry. If R&B, Same Dream, Same Mind, Same Night. If slow rock, SOS. If hip hop, Cheers. If Latin, Light a Flame. If swing/Broadway, Home;Run. If acoustic pop, All My Love. If Afrobeat/Amapiano, Spell. I could go on and on...SEVENTEEN's song list has everything. And it's all kpop.  The '90s-'00s boy bands (at least, here in the US) had their own lanes: strictly pop like nsync or R&B like boyz II men, etc.

author: @JiaPia3
text:
It’s crazy how different they look every comeback. Sometimes I get super confused, but I have The8 (my bias), Woozi, Vernon, Joshua, Hoshi (bias wrecker), S Coups, Jun, Mingyu,and Dino down pat no matter which comeback it is. I want so badly to know them all immediately, but I know it takes time. Any advice would be super helpful. I feel like I can’t call myself a true Carat until I know them all, so I’m STILL a baby. Seventeen puts out some of the best music in K-pop, and I completely stan them 💯! They amaze me. Their sub vocalists could be leads, the boys not in a dance line could be (esp Vernon!), and I’m just amazed they are self produced idols. If they didn’t put in all the effort and relied solely on Pledis, we would have never seen them. It’s sad, but it shows their diligence and determination. God, I’m so happy I got into K-pop (I was really late—my anniversary date is Dec 9, 2018]. Thank you again Carats. You’ve led me to some amazing songs and performances by my top 5 group of all time in and out of the K-pop realm. Seventeen is fantastic. 🥰🤩👍🏾
